messages:
lila-support: FYI — multiple EMEA customers reporting streaming sessions truncating mid-response. They see the SSE stream close, client reconnects, then the resumed stream fails to pick up the remainder.

marco-sre: Which region? any correlation to model or plan?

lila-support: Reported from eu-west-1 and eu-central. Models vary (gptx-small, open-7b). Not tied to a single customer tier.

sarah-cs: One customer pasted logs: they got a final data: chunk, then connection closed with 200, client immediately opened EventSource to /v1/streams/resume and got 401.

priya-runtime: 401 on resume sounds like an auth token lifecycle problem. Do we have auth refresh traces for those requests?

marco-sre: Pulling logs now. Query: "event: sse_close" and "reason: auth_refresh" across eu-west-1 in last 30m.

priya-runtime: Also check the runtime proxy logs for missing Authorization header on upgrade/resume requests. Some clients rely on cookies vs header and our resume path expects header.

marco-sre: Found spike ~1778804922: ~140 stream_resume requests returning 401 in 10m window, user-agent cluster shows variety (node-fetch, browser). Correlation: auth-service returned token_revocation for a short window.

lila-support: Customers say it started right after they updated billing info (card on file changed) but not sure if causal.

billing-bot: Noted a billing webhook retry for 3 customers at 1778804800-1778804900; no account suspensions. Plan change webhook processed successfully. No tokens revoked by billing flow.

priya-runtime: Hmm. Auth-service rotated a signing key earlier as part of scheduled rotation at 1778804600. There was a short replication lag to eu-west-1 caches. During that window some JWTs validated, others did not when the resume request hit a node with new JWKS.

jon-platform: So the resume flow is sensitive to token semantics. Client opens long-lived connection, token expires/refreshes mid-stream, then client reconnect uses new token — should be fine — but if resume path uses cached session id to look up prior stream without validating new token correctly we can get mismatch.

marco-sre: Stack trace sample from proxy: 
```
proxy: sse_resume handler: authenticate() -> jwk_fetch() failed -> 401
runtime: attempt_resume(session=abc123) -> stream not found or unauthorized
```

lila-support: Repro steps from customer (browser):
1) Start streaming generation via EventSource to /v1/streams?model=open-7b with Authorization: Bearer <short-living JWT>
2) Let it run until a token rotation window (~30s later)
3) EventSource disconnects (server closes)
4) Client reconnects automatically with new token; receives 401 on resume endpoint

priya-runtime: The root cause: key rotation + inconsistent session lookup policy + resume requires original session signature. We changed resume auth enforcement in last runtime deploy (1778802000) to tighten security; combination exposed race.

jon-platform: Immediate mitigations? Can we fallback from resume to a full non-resume generation endpoint so the client still gets a completed response?

priya-runtime: Yes. Short term: update gateway to accept resume if either: (a) session id valid and token validates, or (b) token validates for a fresh non-resume /v1/generate call that will produce remaining tokens. Implement flow: on 401 at resume, attempt server-side fallback to create a new completion using stored prompt + offset and stream that back as a normal SSE.

marco-sre: I can push a hotfix to proxy to do that behavior toggle for eu-* regions only. Rolling patch to 3 nodes now.

deploy-bot: deploy request accepted for runtime/gateway hotfix version=1778805033-hotfix-sse-resume-fallback by marco-sre.

marco-sre: Patch live on 3/3 eu-west-1 proxies. Monitoring for resumed streams.

lila-support: Noted one customer reporting restored streaming after ~2m.

priya-runtime: Also adding a small shim: if resume fails with 401, return 202 with a short-lived resume-token and instruct SDK to call /v1/generate?resume_token=<token> which will be accepted even during a key rotation window. Implementing now and will ship patch to SDK docs.

jon-platform: Longer term: make resume auth tolerant to key rotation by using session-bound resume tokens stored server-side (opaque identifiers), not purely JWT signature. Track as ticket RUNTIME-1422.

marco-sre: Added RUNTIME-1422, priority P1 for next sprint. For now I've enabled fallback on eu regions and set alert to fire on >10 resume_401/min.

sarah-cs: I'm drafting a message to affected customers: explain intermittent streaming disruptions in EMEA due to auth key rotation race, outline mitigations (hotfix applied, fallback enabled), recommended client SDK update, and offer to enable region-failover to us-west temporarily if they need immediate stability.

lila-support: Please include repro steps and next steps so support can triage new tickets.

billing-bot: No billing action required. Flagged as incident-impacting for status page.

statusbot: Incident created: "SSE stream resumption failures — EU" at 1778805200; status: investigating. Public note queued.

marco-sre: Postmortem actions assigned: rollback rotation scheduling to non-peak hours, add canary for jwks propagation, add resume token flow, SDK update to re-auth on reconnect.

priya-runtime: Pushed runtime commit that creates opaque resume tokens and docs for SDK auth-on-reconnect. Will open PR for SDK examples.

lila-support: Thanks — closing loop with customers now. If anyone sees a new cluster of 401s ping here.

jon-platform: Also toggled autopin to route streaming traffic from eu-central to eu-west fallback for 10m while caches warm.

marco-sre: Alert rates back down to baseline. Marking mitigated at 1778806420.

lila-support: Final note for thread: customers who experienced truncation may need to re-run prompt; we provided partial transcript and used fallback to stream the remainder in ~60% of cases.

sarah-cs: I'll follow up with the top 3 affected accounts for a waived invoice credit offer and to coordinate SDK rollout.

lila-support: Closing thread but keeping RUNTIME-1422 open.
